question: Assume today is 2026-10-24. You know nothing published after this date. Estimate the number of visitor arrivals to Taiwan (來臺旅客人次) in September 2026, as it will be first reported in the Ministry of Transportation and Communications' (Tourism Administration) monthly statistics on visitor arrivals and outbound departures (來臺旅客及國人出國人數).

target.what: Number of visitor arrivals to Taiwan (來臺旅客人次) during September 2026, as first reported in the Tourism Administration, MOTC monthly statistics on visitor arrivals and outbound departures; counted as arrival events (人次) of visitors entering Taiwan, not unique persons.
target.unit: visitor arrivals (人次) in the month
target.publisher: Tourism Administration, Ministry of Transportation and Communications (MOTC), Taiwan
target.cadence: Monthly; first release normally in the following month
target.caveats: Working interpretation: all inbound visitor arrivals in the monthly table, including foreign nationals and overseas Chinese where reported, excluding outbound ROC citizens and likely excluding transit passengers; repeated entries count separately. First-release values can be revised; if the official

candidates.hypothesis: September 2026 arrivals are anchored by recent 2026 monthly levels and prior September seasonal patterns. A usable relation is: target = recent monthly run-rate × September seasonal index × trend/recovery adjustment, with adjustments for calendar shifts and policy changes.
candidates.data_to_find: Monthly visitor arrivals for Jan-Aug 2026 (or latest months before cutoff), September values for 2023-2025, and full-year or monthly context for 2019/2024/2025. Minimum: latest 3-6 months and same-month prior years; substitute quarterly totals if monthly unavailable.

a.role: Cumulative visitor arrivals to Taiwan for January-September 2026, reported as about 6.175 million; this is the target-period-inclusive cumulative total in the Tourism Administration visitor-arrival series.

b.role: Cumulative visitor arrivals to Taiwan for January-August 2026, precise 5,564,858; this is subtracted to isolate September 2026 arrivals.

methods.rationale: Direct nowcast by differencing the official January-September 2026 cumulative total and the January-August 2026 cumulative total. Because p43 is stated as 'about' 6.175 million, the result inherits rounding uncertainty; p34 is precise. Main failure mode: a vintage or definitional mismatch between the two cumulative releases, although both are from the same monthly visitor-arrival series.

Uses September 2025 arrivals (p1) as the base and scales by the August 2026/August 2025 ratio (p15/p13), transferring the latest observed monthly year-on-year change to September 2026. Main assumption: September 2026 moves at the same year-on-year rate as August 2026. Shared dependence: p1, p13, and p15 all come from the same official monthly arrival series; the main risk is that August's decline is not representative of September.

Uses September 2025 arrivals (p1) and scales by the January-August 2026 / January-August 2025 cumulative ratio (p34/p118), transferring the year-to-date growth rate to September 2026. Main risk: September-specific growth differs from the year-to-date average. p118 is rounded to 5.46 million, adding uncertainty. This signal is separate from m2's August monthly growth signal, though both rely on the same September 2025 base.

assessment.note: These are the strongest reconciliation points. p43 gives an approximate Jan-Sep 2026 cumulative, p44 gives its reported yoy growth, p34 gives a precise Jan-Aug 2026 cumulative, and p5 minus p4 reconstructs Jan-Sep 2025 while p1 anchors September 2025. They agree on roughly 2% YTD growth and imply a September 2026 level near the recent September run-rate. p43 is rounded and p44 comes from the same article, so they are not independent confirmation.

August 2026 total arrivals, August yoy change, August 2025 comparison, source-market levels, foreign/overseas-Chinese components, and air share are mutually consistent. The foreign and overseas-Chinese components reconcile with the total, and p16 matches p15 against p13. These are the best recent monthly level and mix evidence; duplicate copies p176-p182 add no new information.

The 2026 monthly path and cumulative totals are internally consistent: the monthly values reconcile with p18 and p19, p34 extends through August, and p43 is the only point that extends into September. This supports using p34 as the precise January-August base and p43/p44 as the September-relevant cumulative anchor.

Historical September, adjacent-month, and annual totals from the same Taiwan inbound visitor series are consistent across vintages. September 2025 p1 is below August 2025 p13 and well below October 2025 p4, establishing a normal September seasonal dip. p27 and p8 give recent full-year levels; p28/p9 give the pre-pandemic baseline.

January-August 2026 source-market data show a mixed but plausible composition: Japan and Korea slightly down, USA and several Southeast Asian markets up. This is consistent with the roughly 2% cumulative growth and the still-large gap versus pre-pandemic levels in p32 and p36. These points support the level but do not directly provide September monthly arrivals.

Capacity and passenger-flow points are internally consistent for September 2025 and for 2026 Q3/Jan-Aug growth. However, they measure scheduled seats, total passengers, and load factors, not visitor arrivals. Total airport passengers include residents, outbound travellers, and transit/transfer passengers, so a conversion via the visitor share of passenger trips would be required. These points are useful context and cross-checks, not direct substitutes for the target.

Japanese arrivals through September 25, 2026 reached one million, earlier than the late-October timing in 2025. This supports the view that September 2026 was not weaker than the August yoy signal alone would suggest, and it helps justify positive September yoy growth despite negative August yoy.

The 2025 forecast of 8.4 million was below the actual 8.574 million, so annual forecast/target figures should be treated as context or bounds, not as direct September substitutes.

methods.label: m1

a.role: Cumulative visitor arrivals to Taiwan for January-September 2026, reported as about 6.175 million in the Tourism Administration visitor-arrival series.

b.role: Cumulative visitor arrivals to Taiwan for January-August 2026, precise 5,564,858, same visitor-arrival series, subtracted to isolate September 2026.

methods.rationale: Direct cumulative-difference route. p43 is the only kept point extending the 2026 cumulative through September, and p34 is the precise cumulative through August. Subtracting them isolates September 2026. Main risk is p43's rounding and preliminary nature; shared dependence is that both are cumulative totals from the same monthly visitor-arrival system.

methods.label: m2
methods.rationale: Reuses the round-1 yoy_scaling route. Applies the August 2026 versus August 2025 yoy factor in total visitor arrivals to the September 2025 base p1. This assumes August momentum transfers to September. Main risk: August 2026 yoy was negative while the Jan-Sep cumulative was positive, and Mid-Autumn timing differs between 2025 and 2026.

methods.label: m3
methods.rationale: Reuses the round-1 yoy_scaling route. Applies the January-August 2026 versus January-August 2025 cumulative yoy factor to the September 2025 base p1. p34 is precise and p118 is the rounded 2025 comparison. This assumes YTD growth persists into September; it is less sensitive to one-month August noise but may smooth over September-specific calendar or policy effects.

methods.label: m4

a.role: Cumulative visitor arrivals to Taiwan for January-October 2025, used with p4 to reconstruct January-September 2025.

b.role: October 2025 monthly visitor arrivals, subtracted from p5 to reconstruct January-September 2025.

c.role: Reported year-on-year growth rate of January-September 2026 cumulative visitor arrivals versus January-September 2025, applied to the reconstructed 2025 base.

d.role: Precise cumulative visitor arrivals for January-August 2026, subtracted to isolate September 2026.

methods.rationale: Growth-based cumulative reconciliation. January-September 2025 is reconstructed from p5 minus p4, then grown by p44's reported January-September 2026 yoy rate, and p34 is subtracted to isolate September 2026. This uses the growth rate instead of the rounded p43 level, but p43 and p44 are from the same article and remain correlated. Risks: p5/p4 may differ slightly from the comparison base behind p

by_construction: Only URLs leave the searcher (code regex); extractor, judge and final prompts never contain search result titles, snippets or the searcher's text. This holds by construction and is not measured.
residual_risks: The searcher sees post-cutoff search results and chooses which URLs are fetched, so page selection can be conditioned on the answer; only the URLs leave the searcher, and in backtests every fetched page is a snapshot dated <= as_of.
Live pages are used only when as_of is today; in backtests every page is an archived snapshot dated <= as_of.
The leak sentinel only catches registered official values in common formats, not paraphrased or derived numbers.
The model's own training data (knowledge cutoff unpublished) can include history before as_of; it cannot include the target if the target was published after the model's release.
Wayback snapshots are captured by a third party; a snapshot date <= as_of proves the content existed by then.
Assumption values are proposed by the judge model from its own knowledge, which can include the target's history before as_of; code checks their form, not where the number came from.
